sentences.text:
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1054 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kollam, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.08.2007.

According to the petitioner, on 19.08.2007 at about 08.30 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle, he was hit down by a KSRTC bus bearing Registration No.KL- 15-4970 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of accident he sustained serious injuries.
3. The 2nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.2,00,000/-
4.
The KSRTC filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the MACA NO. 2467 OF 2014 2025:KER:31423 offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A8.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.14,914/- and directed the KSRTC to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.Siju Kamalasanan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.Alex Antony Sebastian P.A, the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent/KSRTC.

sentences.text: The Point: In this case the accident is admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as an electrician earning Rs.6,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5,000/-.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in MACA NO. 2467 OF 2014 2025:KER:31423 the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2007 will come to Rs.6,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.6,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2007 will come to Rs.6,000/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.6,000/-.
12.
In the accident the petitioner sustained lacerated injury left eye- brow 5x3 cm, abrasion left side of face, left ring finger and right upper lip.
13. In this case the petitioner has not produced any disability certificate and as such the petitioner is not entitled to get any compensation on the head 'loss of disability'.
14. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.2,500/- being the income for 2 weeks @Rs.5,000/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 2 months.
Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.12,000/- (6,000 x 2 months).
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/-.
Towards 'extra nourishment' only Rs.250/- and towards 'bystander expenses' only Rs.500/- were awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
The petitioner sustained injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 5 days.

Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings'
'bystander expenses' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.10,000/-, Rs.750/- and Rs.750/- respectively.
16. Towards the head 'loss of amenities' no amount was awarded by the Tribunal.
Since the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 5 days, I am inclined to grant Rs.5,000/- on the head 'loss of amenities'.

Towards transportation expenses only Rs.100/-
was awarded and hence it is enhanced to Rs.500/-.
17. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
